_note: V1 hand annotation of bundle_bologna_bcthip, ASME V&V 40. REVISION 2, after D1 found the first version drew every span from Table 1.
_selection_rule: Fixed BEFORE annotating, because the annotator is the same one whose bias is being corrected: take the sentence carrying the most specific evidence -- a figure, a named method, or a named data source -- and never a Table 1 summary cell restating it.
_what_changed: Revision 1 put all 12 spans in sentences 501-525, a contiguous block that is Table 1, in a 989-sentence document. gpt-5 annotating the same document independently placed 19 spans across 221-579 and agreed on the same sentence 0 of 10 times. Reading the pairs showed the disagreement was positional, not substantive: the table cell restates the body finding. Where revision 1 cited 'statistically relevant number of samples used', this cites 'a dataset of 101 calibrated CT scans collected at Rizzoli'. The second is what a credibility rationale needs, because it carries a checkable claim.
